backlog.spec: Replace Morgan bits with all RDKit Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors values (about 210) computed per molecule. Replace NaN and inf with 0 and clip to ±1e6. Keep the RandomForest with max_features 0.3.
backlog.title: RDKit 2D descriptors + RF

backlog.spec: Use Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 1024 bits, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) concatenated with RDKit 2D descriptors (NaN→0, clipped). Use RF with max_features 0.3.
backlog.title: Count Morgan + descriptors concat

backlog.spec: Features are RDKit 2D descriptors (NaN→0, clipped). Model is LGBMRegressor with 500 trees, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, subsample 0.8, subsample_freq 1, colsample_bytree 0.5, min_child_samples 10, n_jobs 8, random_state seed, verbose -1.
backlog.title: LightGBM on descriptors

backlog.spec: Convert train_y to normalized ranks in (0,1) with scipy.stats.rankdata before fitting the RF. The metric is Spearman, so this removes outlier influence. Predictions are used as is.
backlog.title: Rank-transform target

backlog.spec: Swap RandomForestRegressor for ExtraTreesRegressor with 500 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 1.
backlog.title: ExtraTrees instead of RF

backlog.spec: Set N_TREES=600, MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF=3, MAX_FEATURES=0.2 to smooth the predictions.
backlog.title: RF min_samples_leaf 3 and more trees

backlog.spec: Concatenate ECFP count (radius 3, 2048 bits) with FCFP-style counts (the Morgan generator with atom invariants from GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen, radius 2, 1024 bits). Use RF.
backlog.title: ECFP plus FCFP counts

backlog.spec: Concatenate MACCS keys (rdkit MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys), Morgan bits (1024) and RDKit descriptors. Use RF with max_features 0.2.
backlog.title: MACCS + Morgan + descriptors

backlog.spec: Use rdFingerprintGenerator atom-pair counts (fpSize 2048) and topological-torsion counts (fpSize 1024), concatenated with descriptors. Use RF.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and torsion count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Features are descriptors plus Morgan counts (512 bits). Model is CatBoostRegressor with 800 iterations, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, l2_leaf_reg 5, random_seed seed, thread_count 8, verbose 0.
backlog.title: CatBoost on descriptors+counts

backlog.spec: Train an RF on Morgan counts, an LGBM on descriptors and a CatBoost on descriptors. Rank-average their test predictions with scipy rankdata. Rank averaging is suited to Spearman.
backlog.title: RF + LightGBM + CatBoost rank-average ensemble

backlog.spec: Compute Morgan count fingerprints (2048 bits). Compute the MinMax (Tanimoto) kernel matrix with numpy and fit SVR(kernel='precomputed', C=5, epsilon=0.1). Predict with the test-train kernel.
backlog.title: SVR with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Use binary Morgan r2 bits and the Tanimoto kernel. Fit KernelRidge(alpha=1.0, kernel='precomputed') on centered y and predict.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto

backlog.spec: Average the rank-normalized predictions of the RF and a Tanimoto-kernel SVR, both on Morgan counts.
backlog.title: RF and Tanimoto SVR blend

backlog.spec: Winsorize train_y at the 2nd and 98th percentiles before fitting the RF. This reduces outlier leverage.
backlog.title: Winsorize target

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit a quick RF on descriptors plus Morgan counts. Keep the top 300 features by importance, then fit the final RF on them.
backlog.title: Importance-based feature selection

backlog.spec: Use LGBMRegressor with boosting_type='dart', 400 trees, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 15 and colsample 0.4 on descriptors plus Morgan counts (1024). Average 3 seeds.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged dart LightGBM

backlog.spec: Use XGBRegressor with max_depth 4, n_estimators 600, learning_rate 0.03, subsample 0.7, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 3, reg_lambda 5, on descriptors plus Morgan counts (1024).
backlog.title: Shallow XGBoost

backlog.spec: Build a compact feature set: MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, HBD, HBA, RotatableBonds, rings, aromatic rings, fraction sp3 and charge descriptors, plus Morgan counts (512 bits). Use RF with max_features 0.5.
backlog.title: Compact physchem features + counts

backlog.spec: Use Morgan counts with radius 3, 2048 bits and includeChirality=True, via GetMorganGenerator(radius=3, fpSize=2048, includeChirality=True). Use RF.
backlog.title: Chiral radius-3 Morgan

backlog.spec: Take the log1p of Morgan counts (r2, 2048 bits) before RF. Concatenate descriptors.
backlog.title: log1p counts for RF

backlog.spec: Before featurizing, use rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser and Uncharger to standardize molecules. Then use Morgan counts plus descriptors with RF.
backlog.title: Standardize molecules

backlog.spec: Set bootstrap max_samples=0.6, 800 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 2 on Morgan counts plus descriptors, for more decorrelated trees.
backlog.title: RF with max_samples subsampling

backlog.spec: Fit RF and a Ridge on standardized descriptors with alpha 10. Final prediction is 0.7*rank(RF)+0.3*rank(Ridge) among the test molecules.
backlog.title: Ridge stacked with RF

backlog.spec: Standardize descriptors with QuantileTransformer, then average 5 sklearn MLPRegressor models (hidden 128,64, alpha 1e-2, early_stopping) with different seeds. Rank-blend 50/50 with the RF.
backlog.title: MLP ensemble on descriptors

backlog.spec: Add a kNN regressor on Tanimoto distance, using the weighted mean of y over the top 7 neighbours on Morgan bits. Blend 30% with the RF by rank.
backlog.title: Tanimoto kNN blend

backlog.spec: Add Avalon count fingerprints (pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP, 1024 bits) and ErG (rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint) to the Morgan counts plus descriptors. Use RF.
backlog.title: Avalon and ErG fingerprints

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, hold out 15% of training molecules grouped by Murcko scaffold. Fit LGBM with early stopping on it, then refit on all data with the best iteration count. Use descriptors plus Morgan counts.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped early stopping LightGBM

backlog.spec: Use LGBMRegressor(objective='huber', alpha=1.0) on the standardized target, 500 trees, lr 0.03, num_leaves 15, colsample 0.4, on descriptors plus Morgan counts.
backlog.title: Huber-loss LightGBM

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace y with its normalized rank (rankdata(y)/len(y)) before fitting both the XGBoost and the SVR (SVR standardization still applies afterwards). Since the metric is Spearman, this removes the influence of target outliers. Keep the final rank-average blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Rank-transform target for all models

backlog.spec: Add a CatBoostRegressor (depth 6, 800 iterations, learning_rate 0.04, l2_leaf_reg 5, rsm 0.2, thread_count 8, random_seed=seed, verbose 0) trained on xgb_features(train). Reuse the feature matrices already computed (compute them once per split). Blend the three rank-normalized predictions (XGB, SVR, CatBoost) with equal weights.
backlog.title: Add CatBoost on descriptors+counts as third blend member

backlog.spec: Compute atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048) and a min/max Tanimoto kernel on them. Average this kernel with the Morgan Tanimoto kernel (0.5/0.5) and fit one precomputed SVR on the averaged kernel, replacing the current SVR. Vectorize the kernel for speed if needed.
backlog.title: Multi-kernel SVR: add atom-pair count kernel

backlog.spec: Replace the SVR with sklearn KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.3) on the Morgan count min/max Tanimoto kernel, with centered target. Keep the XGB branch and the rank blend. Kernel ridge is smoother than epsilon-SVR and might rank better.
backlog.title: Gaussian process / kernel ridge on Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Train 5 XGBRegressor models with different random_state values (seed*10+i) and subsample/colsample randomness, with n_estimators 400 each, and average their predictions for the tree branch. This reduces variance of the tree branch while leaving the SVR branch unchanged.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged XGBoost

backlog.spec: Change the final return to 0.4*rank(p_xgb)/n + 0.6*rank(p_svr)/n. The SVR on fingerprints generalizes across scaffolds well; test whether giving it more weight helps. Single constant change.
backlog.title: Blend weight tuning 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB

backlog.spec: In xgb_features, drop descriptor columns that are constant on the training set and Morgan columns that are nonzero in fewer than 10 training molecules (compute the mask in fit_predict and apply to test). Also drop one of each descriptor pair with abs correlation above 0.95. This reduces noise features for the XGB branch with colsample 0.3.
backlog.title: Feature selection by variance and correlation on descriptors

backlog.spec: Add a third branch: sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden layers (256,64), alpha 1e-2, early_stopping True, max_iter 300) bagged over 5 seeds on QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal') scaled RDKit descriptors. Average their predictions, rank-normalize, and add to the blend with equal weight.
backlog.title: Small MLP ensemble on standardized descriptors as extra member

backlog.spec: Append Avalon count fingerprint (rdkit.Avalon.pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP, nBits 1024) and ErG fingerprint (rdkit.Chem.rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint) to the xgb_features matrix. Leave the SVR kernel unchanged.
backlog.title: Add Avalon and ErG fingerprints to the XGB features

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, produce out-of-fold predictions for XGB and SVR on the training set using 4-fold GroupKFold grouped by Murcko scaffold (via MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles). Fit a non-negative LinearRegression on the OOF ranks to learn blend weights, then apply it to the test predictions from models fit on the full training set. Fall back to equal weights if weights degenerate.
backlog.title: Ridge-stacked blend via inner CV

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, change the final return to 0.6*rankdata(p_svr)/len(p_svr) + 0.4*rankdata(p_rf)/len(p_rf). No other changes. Tests whether the kernel model deserves more weight.
backlog.title: Replicate-safe blend weight 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB

backlog.spec: Change the SVR hyperparameters to C=1.0 and epsilon=0.05 (smaller C gives a smoother fit on the rank-normalized target). Keep everything else the same. If it helps, a later slot can try C=15.
backlog.title: Tune SVR C and epsilon on rank target

backlog.spec: Replace the XGBRegressor with CatBoostRegressor(iterations=800, depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, l2_leaf_reg=5, rsm=0.3, loss_function='RMSE', random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0) trained on xgb_features and the rank target. Keep the SVR and the rank blend. CatBoost's ordered boosting often does better on small data.
backlog.title: CatBoost replaces XGBoost on descriptors+Morgan

backlog.spec: Fit 5 XGBRegressors with seeds seed..seed+4, using the same hyperparameters and subsample 0.7, and average their predictions before ranking. Compute the xgb_features matrices once and reuse them. This reduces variance at a small time cost.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged XGBoost (5 seeds)

backlog.spec: Build a second kernel from FCFP4 count fingerprints (Morgan generator with atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), radius 2, 2048 bits). Average its min/max kernel with the existing ECFP kernel before fitting the SVR. This adds pharmacophore-level similarity that ECFP lacks.
backlog.title: Add Avalon, ErG and FCFP features to the SVR kernel

backlog.spec: Compute RDKit descriptors, apply QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal'), and drop descriptors with near-zero variance. Fit SVR(kernel='rbf', C=3, gamma='scale') on the rank target. Add its rank-normalized prediction as a third equally weighted blend member next to the XGB and Tanimoto SVR predictions.
backlog.title: Descriptor RBF kernel SVR as third member

backlog.spec: Fit the XGB once on all features. Keep the top 300 features by gain importance, refit on this subset, and predict. Use the same seed. This cuts noise from the roughly 1200 mostly sparse features.
backlog.title: Feature selection for XGB by importance

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform rank target with scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n), clipped to [-2.5, 2.5]. Use it for both the XGB and the SVR (the SVR already standardizes it). This puts more emphasis on the middle of the distribution than the uniform rank does.
backlog.title: Winsorized rank target with a Gaussian transform

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run 5-fold GroupKFold on the training set, grouped by Murcko scaffold, to get out-of-fold XGB and SVR predictions. Fit a non-negative LinearRegression (positive=True) on their ranks against the rank target to learn the blend weights. Then fit both models on all the training data and combine their test ranks with the learned weights. This replaces the fixed 1:1 blend. Keep the code compact.
backlog.title: Monotone-pairwise fine-tune: stacked second-stage on out-of-fold predictions

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, compute xgb_features for train and test once, then fit 5 XGBRegressor models with the current hyperparameters but random_state=seed+k for k in 0..4, and average their predictions to get p_rf. Keep the SVR and the rank blend unchanged. This reduces variance of the tree branch. Check the job stays under 10 minutes.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged XGBoost (5 seeds)

backlog.spec: Change the final return to 0.6*rankdata(p_svr)/len(p_svr) + 0.4*rankdata(p_rf)/len(p_rf). Nothing else changes. The SVR on Tanimoto kernels may be the stronger member, so this tests the blend weighting.
backlog.title: Blend weights 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB

backlog.spec: Change the SVR to C=10.0 and epsilon=0.05, targeting the rank-transformed standardized target. Leave everything else unchanged. If the job is stable, this tests whether the kernel model is under-regularized or over-regularized.
backlog.title: Tune SVR C and epsilon

backlog.spec: Add an atom-pair count fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) for train and test. Compute the min/max tanimoto kernel on it and average it with the Morgan kernel (0.5/0.5) for both train-train and test-train matrices, then fit the SVR on the averaged kernel. Leave the XGB branch unchanged.
backlog.title: Multi-kernel SVR: average Morgan and atom-pair count Tanimoto kernels

backlog.spec: Build a second kernel from concatenated Avalon count (1024) and feature-Morgan (useFeatures invariants, radius 2, 1024 bits) count vectors. Average it with the existing Morgan min/max kernel, then fit the SVR on the average. The XGB branch is unchanged.
backlog.title: Add Avalon, ErG and FCFP counts to the SVR kernel

backlog.spec: Replace the rank/n target with scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n), clipped to [-2.5, 2.5]. Use it for both XGB and SVR; the SVR's standardization stays. This changes the loss emphasis toward the center and away from the extreme ranks.
backlog.title: Winsorized Gaussian-rank target

backlog.spec: Fit a first XGBRegressor on the full feature matrix. Keep the top 400 features by gain importance and refit the final XGB on only those columns, using the same hyperparameters. Selection is done inside fit_predict on the training data only. Predictions come from the refit model.
backlog.title: Importance-based feature selection for XGB

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, run 5-fold KFold on the training set (seeded) to get out-of-fold rank predictions from XGB and SVR. Fit a non-negative linear regression (scipy.optimize.nnls or sklearn LinearRegression(positive=True)) on those two columns to the rank target. Refit both models on all the training data and combine the test rank predictions with the learned weights. This replaces the equal-weight blend.
backlog.title: Stacked second-stage via inner scaffold-free CV

backlog.spec: Append a feature-Morgan (FCFP-like, useFeatures=True via GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen, radius 2, 1024 bits count) fingerprint to xgb_features alongside the existing features. Everything else is unchanged. This tests whether pharmacophoric atom invariants add signal for the trees.
backlog.title: Count-Morgan radius 3 feature-invariant added to XGB

backlog.spec: Change the XGB to max_depth=6, n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.02, subsample=0.6, colsample_bytree=0.2, min_child_weight=5, reg_lambda=10, reg_alpha=0.5. This is a bolder regularized variant of the tree branch, to check whether more interaction depth helps when it is coupled with heavier column subsampling.
backlog.title: Deeper trees with stronger subsampling in XGB

backlog.spec: Replace y = rankdata/n with scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n) clipped to [-2,2] for both XGB and SVR (SVR still standardizes). Tests whether a Gaussian-shaped target helps the regressors.
backlog.title: Winsorized Gaussian-rank target

backlog.spec: Change XGBRegressor to max_depth=6, subsample=0.5, colsample_bytree=0.2, min_child_weight=5, n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.02, reg_lambda=10. Tests a higher-capacity, more randomized tree model.
backlog.title: Deeper XGB with stronger subsampling

backlog.spec: In xgb_features, add a second Morgan count generator with radius 3 and fpSize 1024 and append its counts to the concatenated feature row. Keep all else the same.
backlog.title: Morgan radius-3 counts added to XGB features

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, make 5-fold inner KFold (seeded, shuffled) out-of-fold predictions of XGB and SVR on the training set. Fit a non-negative LinearRegression (positive=True) on the two OOF rank vectors and use its weights to blend the test predictions. Compute features once to save time.
backlog.title: Stacked second stage via inner CV

backlog.spec: Add a LightGBM model with boosting_type='dart', 400 trees, lr 0.05, num_leaves 15, colsample_bytree 0.3, subsample 0.7 with subsample_freq 1, on the xgb_features matrix. Average 3 seeds, then rank-blend equally as a third member with XGB and SVR.
backlog.title: Seed-bagged dart LightGBM third member

backlog.spec: Add a third member: SVR with kernel built as exp(-gamma*(1-minmax_tanimoto)) from the Avalon count fingerprint (1024 bits) alone, gamma=2, C=5. Rank-blend equally with the other two members.
backlog.title: Count-feature log1p with PCA-free RBF SVR on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Compute Murcko scaffold per training molecule with rdkit MurckoScaffold. Pass sample_weight = 1/sqrt(scaffold count) to XGB fit and to SVR fit (sample_weight argument). This reduces dominance of large scaffold families and may help generalization to unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware sample weighting

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, change the final return to 0.6*rankdata(p_svr)/len(p_svr) + 0.4*rankdata(p_rf)/len(p_rf). No other change.
backlog.title: Blend weight 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB

backlog.spec: Build the SVR kernel as the product (elementwise) sqrt of the Morgan min/max kernel K and an RBF kernel on quantile-scaled, clipped RDKit descriptors, K_final = K * exp(-gamma*d2) with gamma = 1/(n_features*2). Use it in the existing SVR in place of K alone.
backlog.title: Stacking-free second SVR on descriptors with Tanimoto product kernel

backlog.spec: Set learning_rate=0.015, n_estimators=1200 in XGBRegressor and add gamma=0.1 regularization. Keep other params.
backlog.title: Lower XGB learning rate with more trees and early-stopping-free shrinkage

backlog.spec: After fitting the SVR on the training set, compute 5-fold inner out-of-fold SVR predictions, and replace the rank target for XGB with 0.7*y + 0.3*oof_pred_rank. This is a distillation-style label smoothing that denoises XGB targets. Use KFold with the seed.
backlog.title: Target noise smoothing via pseudo-label averaging

backlog.spec: Train 8 SVRs, each on a random 80% subsample of training molecules (seeded) using the precomputed kernel sub-blocks, and average their rank predictions for the SVR branch. Reduces variance of the kernel model.
backlog.title: Bagged SVR over bootstrap subsamples with feature-count dropout

backlog.spec: Replace K with K**2 (elementwise power of the min/max Tanimoto kernel) in the SVR for both train and test kernels, sharpening similarity. Keep C=5.
backlog.title: Add Gaussian-process-style SVR with power-transformed Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Remove from xgb_features the descriptor columns that depend on molecule size only through raw counts (those starting with 'fr_' and 'Num'), keeping fingerprints and continuous descriptors, to reduce overfitting on scaffold-shifted folds.
backlog.title: Test-time augmentation with randomized SMILES-invariant descriptors dropped

backlog.spec: Change the SVR to C=2.0 and epsilon=0.05 on the rank-standardized target (currently C=5, epsilon=0.1). Keep everything else the same. If you want one change only, keep these two values together.
backlog.title: Tune SVR C and epsilon

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, raise the min/max Tanimoto kernel matrices to the power 2 elementwise (K**2, for both train-train and test-train) before the SVR. This sharpens similarity and acts like a different kernel width. Keep C=5.
backlog.title: Power-transformed Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Replace the single SVR with an average of 8 SVRs. Each is fit on a random 80% subsample of the training rows, drawn with np.random.RandomState(seed+i). Compute the train-train kernel once and slice it for each subsample. Average the predictions before ranking. This reduces variance in the kernel model.
backlog.title: Bagged SVR over bootstrap subsamples

backlog.spec: Smooth the training target with neighbors. After computing the rank target y, replace it with 0.7*y + 0.3*(Tanimoto-similarity-weighted mean of y over the top 5 nearest training neighbors, excluding the molecule itself), using the Morgan min/max kernel already computed. Fit both models on this smoothed target. This reduces label noise.
backlog.title: Second-stage pairwise-free rank-averaged target smoothing

backlog.spec: Apply np.log1p to the Morgan count matrices Xtr and Xte before computing the min/max Tanimoto kernel. This compresses large counts so that common substructures dominate less.
backlog.title: Log1p counts in the SVR kernel

backlog.spec: Build the SVR kernel as the average of min/max kernels from Morgan counts at radius 1 (2048 bits) and radius 3 (2048 bits). The average covers both small fragments and large environments. Use it in place of the current radius-2 kernel.
backlog.title: Mixed-radius Morgan kernel

backlog.spec: Set XGBRegressor to max_depth=3, n_estimators=1000, learning_rate=0.03, colsample_bytree=0.2, subsample=0.7, min_child_weight=5, reg_lambda=10. This is a bolder move toward a simpler, more regularized model.
backlog.title: XGB with extra-shallow depth 3 and many more trees

backlog.spec: Fit 4 XGBoost models on the same rows, each with a different seed and colsample_bytree=0.15 (instead of one model at 0.3), with max_depth=4 and n_estimators=400. Average their predictions before ranking. This gives a more diverse ensemble than the seed-only bagging tried before.
backlog.title: Random-subspace XGB bagging over feature groups

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, change the SVR hyperparameters from C=5.0, epsilon=0.1 to C=2.0, epsilon=0.05 (the target is standardized rank). Keep everything else unchanged. One run only; this is a pure hyperparameter shift toward smoother, less regularized fits.
backlog.title: Tune SVR C and epsilon

backlog.spec: Replace the single SVR with an average of 8 SVRs, each fit on a random 80% subsample of the training rows (use np.random.RandomState(seed)). Compute the full train kernel once and slice it per subsample, and slice the test-vs-train kernel the same way. Average the 8 predictions, then rank-blend with XGB as before.
backlog.title: Bagged SVR on bootstrap subsamples

backlog.spec: Before fitting, replace the rank target y with 0.7*y + 0.3*(Tanimoto-weighted mean of y over the 5 nearest training neighbors, excluding self), using the existing min/max kernel on Morgan counts. Fit both models on this smoothed target. This reduces label noise.
backlog.title: Pseudo-label smoothing of target

backlog.spec: Train 4 XGB models. Each uses a different feature group: (a) descriptors+Morgan, (b) descriptors+Avalon, (c) descriptors+ErG+Morgan, (d) all features. Use a different seed for each. Average their predictions before rank blending with the SVR. Slice the columns of the existing feature matrix by index ranges.
backlog.title: Random-subspace XGB bagging

backlog.spec: Add a third blend member: an XGBRegressor with the same parameters trained only on the RDKit descriptor columns (the first len(Descriptors.descList) columns of xgb_features). Rank-average it with weights XGB-full 0.35, SVR 0.45, descriptor-XGB 0.2.
backlog.title: Rank-averaged blend with a descriptor-only XGB

backlog.spec: Replace XGBRegressor with XGBRanker (objective rank:pairwise) using a single query group over all training rows. Use integer relevance labels from 0 to 30 obtained by binning the rank target. Keep the other hyperparameters. Rank-blend with the SVR as before. This directly optimizes ordering, which is what Spearman scores.
backlog.title: Pairwise-rank objective XGB

backlog.spec: For the Morgan count kernel, compute the fingerprints from 3 random atom-order SMILES per molecule via Chem.MolToSmiles(m, doRandom=True), seeded by the seed argument. Use the mean count vector. Morgan counts should be invariant to atom order, so first check this is not a no-op. Instead, make the augmentation a count-dropout version: for each of 3 copies of the training set, randomly zero 10% of the nonzero count bits. Fit the SVR on the 3x stacked set and predict on the unmodified test set.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES augmentation for SVR kernel

backlog.spec: Train XGB with 800 trees and a learning_rates callback (xgboost.callback.LearningRateScheduler) that decays from 0.06 to 0.005 along a cosine schedule. Keep depth 4 and the other parameters. This is a schedule change, not a retune of depth.
backlog.title: Cosine-decayed XGB learning rate

backlog.spec: For the SVR kernel features, average Morgan count vectors is invariant already, so instead augment with different atom-order-invariant variants: compute Morgan counts with useBondTypes=False variant (generator with includeChirality False and a bond-invariant-free atom invariant generator via GetMorganAtomInvGen) and average the min/max kernel of the standard ECFP4 with this generalized-atom-invariant kernel before fitting the SVR.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES augmented count kernel

backlog.spec: After computing the rank target y, replace it by 0.7*y + 0.3*(Tanimoto-kernel-weighted mean of y over the 5 nearest training neighbors excluding self, using the Morgan min/max kernel already computed). Fit both XGB and SVR on this smoothed target. Predictions are still ranked.
backlog.title: Pseudo-label smoothing of target

backlog.spec: Append to xgb_features a few engineered features: Crippen logP times TPSA, logP squared, fraction of sp3 carbons times MolWt, number of rotatable bonds divided by heavy atoms, and counts of SMARTS for common metabolic soft spots (aromatic methoxy, N-methyl, benzylic CH, ester, unsubstituted phenyl). Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Hepatocyte-clearance-aware physchem interactions

backlog.spec: Fit three SVRs on the same Morgan min/max kernel with C=1, 5, 25, rank-average their predictions into a single SVR component (equal weights), then blend with XGB 50/50 as before.
backlog.title: Rank-average of SVR on several kernels with different C

backlog.spec: Add a third rank-blend member: solve (K + 0.5*I)^-1 (y - mean) on the Morgan count min/max kernel via scipy.linalg.solve with assume_a='pos', predict with test-train kernel. Weight the rank blend as XGB 0.4, SVR 0.4, GP 0.2.
backlog.title: Gaussian process regression on Tanimoto kernel with noise

backlog.spec: After producing the blended prediction for test molecules, smooth it transductively: new_pred = 0.8*pred + 0.2*mean of pred over the 3 most similar test molecules (Morgan min/max kernel among test molecules, excluding self, if similarity>0.5, else keep own). Return ranks.
backlog.title: Monotone isotonic calibration-free pairwise stacking by test-time kNN neighbor rank smoothing

backlog.spec: In fit_predict change the SVR to C=10.0 and epsilon=0.05 (rank target standardized). Keep everything else unchanged. Tests whether the kernel model is under-regularized or over-regularized.
backlog.title: Tune SVR C and epsilon

backlog.spec: Replace the SVR by closed-form GP/kernel regression: K = min/max kernel on Morgan counts, predict with K_test_train @ solve(K + 0.5*I, y - mean) + mean. Try noise 0.5 on the rank target. Keep the rank blend with XGB.
backlog.title: Gaussian process regression on Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: For the XGB branch, build features for test molecules from 5 randomized SMILES variants (Chem.MolToSmiles(m, doRandom=True) with seeded random state via np seed) in addition to canonical, predict each, and average. Descriptors are mostly invariant, so only fingerprints that are atom-order-sensitive change. Keep the training unchanged.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES test-time augmentation for XGB

backlog.spec: Train XGBoost via xgboost.train with a learning-rate callback (LearningRateScheduler) decaying cosine from 0.06 to 0.005 over 600 rounds, with the same depth, subsample, colsample and regularization parameters. Predict with the final booster.
backlog.title: Cosine-decayed XGB learning rate

backlog.spec: Fit three SVRs on the same Tanimoto kernel with C=1, 5, 25, rank-average their predictions into one SVR member, then blend with XGB 50/50 as before.
backlog.title: Multi-kernel SVR average at different C

backlog.spec: After the blend, compute min/max Tanimoto similarity between test molecules and also use train similarity; replace each test prediction with 0.8*own + 0.2*similarity-weighted mean of predictions of its 3 nearest other test molecules (similarity>0.5 only, otherwise keep own). Apply final rank.
backlog.title: Test-time neighbor rank smoothing

backlog.spec: Bold: train a LightGBM on pairs of training molecules (sample 40000 random pairs), features = x_i - x_j on the xgb_features matrix, target = y_i - y_j (rank target). To predict, score each test molecule against 100 random training anchors, and prediction = mean(y_anchor + pred_delta). Rank-blend as a third member with weight 1/3.
backlog.title: Pairwise-difference Siamese-free GBM on descriptor deltas

backlog.spec: Build 6 min/max kernels each from a random 70% subset of Morgan count columns (seeded), fit an SVR per kernel, and average their ranks as the SVR member. Provides random-subspace diversity for the kernel model.
backlog.title: Bagged feature-count dropout in SVR kernel

backlog.spec: Cluster training molecules with Butina on Tanimoto distance 0.2 (rdkit) of Morgan bits; for clusters of size>=2 replace each rank target by 0.8*own + 0.2*cluster mean rank. Fit both models on the smoothed target. Only near-duplicates are smoothed, unlike the earlier kNN smoothing.
backlog.title: Noise-robust target by clustered rank averaging

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, for the test molecules only, compute xgb_features on the canonical SMILES plus 4 randomized SMILES variants per molecule (Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, doRandom=True, canonical=False), with random state set from seed via Chem.SetUseLegacyStereoPerception-free approach: just seed numpy and use doRandom). Average the XGBoost predictions across the variants before ranking. Note that count fingerprints and most descriptors are invariant, so this only perturbs minor features; if the output is identical, instead add Gaussian noise (sd 0.02 of column std) to the test features for 5 copies and average. Leave training unchanged.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES test-time augmentation

backlog.spec: Replace the single SVR with three SVRs sharing the same precomputed Tanimoto min/max kernel but with C in {1, 5, 20} and epsilon 0.1. Rank-normalize each prediction and average them into one SVR rank, then blend 50/50 with the XGB rank as now. Compute the kernel matrices once.
backlog.title: Multi-C SVR rank average

backlog.spec: Replace the single SVR fit with 10 SVRs, each fit on a random 80% subsample of the training rows (without replacement, rng seeded from seed). Slice the precomputed train-train kernel matrix for each fit and use the matching test-train columns for prediction. Average the 10 predictions, then rank as before. Use the same C=5, epsilon=0.1.
backlog.title: Bagged SVR on bootstrap subsamples

backlog.spec: Cluster the training molecules with Butina clustering on Morgan Tanimoto distance (threshold 0.35, computed from bit fingerprints). Replace each training rank target with 0.8*own rank + 0.2*mean rank of its cluster (singletons unchanged). Fit both XGB and SVR on this smoothed target. Re-normalize to ranks afterward.
backlog.title: Cluster-averaged noise-robust target

backlog.spec: Build 5 min/max Tanimoto kernels, each from a random 60% subset of the 2048 Morgan count columns chosen with a seed-based rng. Fit an SVR on each (C=5, epsilon=0.1), rank and average the 5 predictions to get the SVR component. Keep the XGB branch unchanged.
backlog.title: Dropout-style random-subspace SVR kernel ensemble

backlog.spec: Use one SVR on the geometric mean (elementwise sqrt of the product) of the Morgan count min/max kernel and the Avalon count (1024 bits) min/max kernel, instead of the Morgan kernel alone. Compute the kernels for train-train and test-train. Keep C=5 and epsilon=0.1.
backlog.title: Second-order Morgan-count kernel product with Avalon

backlog.spec: Add a third rank-blend member: a LightGBM (300 trees, lr 0.05, 15 leaves, colsample 0.3) trained on 40000 random training pairs where the features are x_i - x_j from xgb_features and the target is rank_i - rank_j. For each test molecule, predict the difference against 200 random training anchors, then score = mean(pred_diff + anchor_rank). Blend weights 0.4 XGB, 0.4 SVR, 0.2 pairwise. Seed all random choices from the seed argument.
backlog.title: Pairwise-difference LightGBM as third member with ECFP6 kernel

backlog.spec: Weight the training samples in the XGB and SVR fits (via sample_weight) by 1 + 1.0*|rank - 0.5|*2. This gives the tails of the target more weight, since Spearman is sensitive to getting the extremes ordered correctly. Pass the weights to XGBRegressor.fit and SVR.fit.
backlog.title: Target-quantile-stratified sample weights

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, fit three SVRs on the same precomputed Morgan count min/max Tanimoto kernel with C=1, 5 and 20 (epsilon 0.1). Compute the train-train and test-train kernels once. Rank-normalize each SVR's predictions and average them into a single p_svr. Leave the XGB branch and the final 1:1 rank blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Multi-C SVR rank average

backlog.spec: Augment the SVR training set only. For each training molecule, generate 2 extra Morgan count vectors from randomized atom-order SMILES (Chem.MolToSmiles with doRandom=True, seeded via random.seed or np.random from the seed argument), then re-parse them. Give the copies the same rank target. Fit the SVR on the enlarged kernel and predict test molecules from the canonical features. Leave XGB unchanged.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES augmented SVR training

backlog.spec: After computing the final blended rank score for test molecules, compute the Morgan min/max Tanimoto kernel between test molecules (test-test). For each test molecule, set final = 0.8*own + 0.2*similarity^3-weighted mean of the scores of its top-3 most similar other test molecules, but only when similarity > 0.6. Otherwise keep the own score. Return the result.
backlog.title: Test-time neighbor rank smoothing

backlog.spec: After fitting XGB, call model.apply(X) to get leaf indices for train and test. Build a kernel as the fraction of trees in which two molecules share a leaf (loop over chunks, or use one-hot of leaves with a sparse dot product divided by n_trees). Fit a third SVR (C=5) on this precomputed kernel and add it to the rank blend with weight 0.5, compared with 1 for each of the other two. The leaf indices come from the training set, so this is an in-sample embedding. Keep XGB's subsample at 0.7.
backlog.title: Hybrid SVR with kernel on the XGB leaf embeddings

backlog.spec: Pass sample_weight to XGB.fit and SVR.fit. The weight is 1 + 0.5*|y_rank - 0.5|*2, so extreme-clearance molecules count more. The rank target y is already in [0,1]. Test whether emphasizing the tails improves Spearman. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Quantile-stratified sample weights

backlog.spec: Compute 5-fold inner out-of-fold SVR predictions on the train set, using slices of the precomputed kernel. Append the OOF predictions as one extra feature column to the XGB feature matrix. For test, use the SVR trained on all train data as that feature. Fit XGB on the augmented features and use its output directly, blended 50/50 by rank with the SVR as before.
backlog.title: Two-stage residual XGB on SVR out-of-fold predictions

backlog.spec: For the XGB branch only, add 1000 synthetic training rows. Each is a convex combination lam*xi+(1-lam)*xj of two random training rows, with lam~Beta(0.4,0.4). It gets the same combination of the rank targets. Draw the pairs only from molecules with similar targets (|yi-yj|<0.2), using RandomState(seed). Fit XGB on the original and synthetic rows together.
backlog.title: Descriptor-space adversarial-free mixup augmentation

backlog.spec: Replace the SVR kernel K (min/max Tanimoto) with K2 = exp(-3*(1-K)). Compute it on the same Morgan count features, for both the train-train and test-train matrices. Use SVR C=10. Leave the rest of the blend unchanged.
backlog.title: Atom-environment substructure-count SVR kernel with Gaussian-of-distance transform

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, build the SVR kernel as the average of three min/max Tanimoto count kernels: Morgan radius 2 (existing), Morgan radius 3 counts (2048 bits), and FCFP4 (useFeatureInvariants via MorganFeatureAtomInvGen, radius 2, 2048 bits). Compute each kernel for train-train and test-train, average, and pass to the precomputed SVR. Leave XGB unchanged.
backlog.title: Replicate-confirm incumbent with ECFP6+FCFP4 averaged kernel

backlog.spec: Add a small sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden 256,64, alpha 1e-2, early_stopping) trained on Morgan count log1p features (2048) to predict the rank target; average 5 seeds and add as a third rank-blend member with weight 0.5 relative to 1.0 for XGB and SVR. Use seed for all randomness.
backlog.title: Rank-target multi-task via auxiliary descriptor targets for MLP

backlog.spec: Compute the Morgan min/max kernel once, then fit three SVRs with C=1, 5, 20 (epsilon 0.1) and replace p_svr with the mean of their rank-normalized predictions. Keep XGB branch unchanged.
backlog.title: Rank-average SVR over multiple C values

backlog.spec: After computing the final blended score for test molecules, replace it with 0.8*own + 0.2*similarity-weighted mean of blended scores of the top-3 most similar test molecules (min/max Tanimoto on Morgan counts, only neighbors with similarity>0.5). Use the already computed count features for test.
backlog.title: Test-time kNN neighbor rank smoothing

backlog.spec: Augment the SVR training set with 500 synthetic samples: pick random pairs of training molecules with Tanimoto similarity >0.4, average their count vectors and their rank targets with lambda~Uniform(0.3,0.7). Concatenate to training data and fit the precomputed-kernel SVR on the enlarged set; XGB unchanged.
backlog.title: Mixup augmentation in kernel space for SVR

backlog.spec: Weight training samples by 1+2*|y_rank-0.5| (extremes of clearance emphasized) in both XGBoost fit (sample_weight) and SVR fit (sample_weight). Leave everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Quantile-stratified sample weights

backlog.spec: Add a second XGBoost (same hyperparameters) trained on RDKit descriptors plus atom-pair count (1024 bits) and topological torsion count (1024 bits) fingerprints. Blend three members by rank with weights 0.25 for each XGB and 0.5 for SVR.
backlog.title: Extra XGB with different feature view (atom-pair + torsion counts)

backlog.spec: Add rdMolDescriptors autocorrelation features (CalcAUTOCORR2D, MQN via rdMolDescriptors.MQNs_, and BCUT2D via rdMolDescriptors.BCUT2D) to xgb_features, with nan_to_num. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Gaussian-process-free: SVR on 3D-free graph-distance descriptors (autocorrelation)

backlog.spec: Fit 8 SVRs each using a random 60% of the Morgan fingerprint bit columns (random column subset per model, seeded) to compute the min/max kernel, and average their rank predictions as p_svr. Kernels are computed per subset on the fly.
backlog.title: Two-fold stochastic weight of SVR via DART-style kernel dropout

backlog.spec: Generate 5-fold inner out-of-fold blended predictions on the training set (XGB with 300 trees to save time, SVR), fit sklearn IsotonicRegression mapping blended OOF score to rank target, and apply it to the test blend. This is mostly rank-preserving, so instead use the OOF blend weights chosen by grid search over w in {0.3..0.7} maximizing Spearman, and use that w for the final blend.
backlog.title: Rank-target monotone isotonic post-calibration of the blend

incumbent.description: Append Avalon count fingerprint (1024 bits) and ErG fingerprint to the XGB feature matrix, leaving the SVR kernel unchanged.

memo:
Helped: rank-blending diverse families (RF + Tanimoto SVR, 0.5407 from the 0.6103 baseline), then XGBoost on descriptors plus Morgan counts (0.5195), a rank-transformed target (0.4994), and Avalon count + ErG features in XGB (0.4718, the incumbent). The incumbent is a single run with noise sd ~0.0070, so it is unconfirmed.

Did not help, or stayed within noise: kNN, ExtraTrees, KernelRidge, GP, LightGBM, Ridge, MLP, MACCS, CatBoost swaps, seed-bagged XGB, feature selection, XGB retuning, stacking, blend weights, target smoothing and sample weights. Most results landed within about ±0.006 of the incumbent.

Near-noise gains: ECFP4/ECFP6/FCFP4 averaged kernel 0.4649, pairwise-difference LightGBM 0.4653, FCFP4 kernel 0.4637/0.4771, ECFP6 kernel 0.4658, CatBoost third member 0.4678.

Next: replicate 0.4718 first. Then combine the multi-radius kernel (0.4649) with the pairwise LightGBM (0.4653) as a third member. Check the abort list first, since many ideas are repeats.
